title: ‘From BLOOM to Voice of Nature and Drums of India’: Cultural Performances Bring 57th IFFI Closing Ceremony to Life
subtitle: Three Cultural Performances Celebrate Stories That Take Root and Blossom Without Borders in One Rhythm
body_text:
Posted On: 28 NOV 2026 9:00PM by PIB Mumbai Release ID: 2343251 Views: 90 A A Print Share X Facebook Instagram WhatsApp Copy Article Link
Read in: English Gujarati Urdu हिन्दी Malayalam
Goa, 28 November 2026 A celebration of imagination, nature and cultural diversity marked the closing ceremony of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026 in Goa, as three cultural performances brought the festival’s theme, ‘Stories Without Borders’, to life. The celebrations opened with ‘ BLOOM: Stories that Take Root, Stories Without Borders ’, a poetic dance presentation drawing parallels between the blossoming of flowers and the journey of stories. Just as a flower unfolds petal by petal, revealing new colours and perspectives, stories emerge from diverse cultures and experiences to connect people across boundaries. Blending Indian and Western dance traditions with contemporary expressions and aerial dance, the performance featured dancers in rose-petal-inspired costumes. The arrival of butterflies symbolised the spread of creativity, freedom and the limitless possibilities of imagination. The evening moved from the imagery of a blooming flower to the sounds of the natural world with ‘ When Nature Speaks, Stories Without Borders ’, a performance by internationally acclaimed vocal artist Mystic Papizh. Known for his four-octave vocal range, Papizh recreated the rustling of leaves, birdsong at dawn and the flow of rivers through his voice. A four-time Golden Buzzer recipient across international editions of Got Talent , he brought together nature-inspired sounds, ancient spiritual traditions and contemporary vocal art in a musical expression of peace and harmony between humanity and nature. The celebrations culminated with ‘ Drums of India’ , a musical fusion bringing together rhythms from different parts of India and the world. Traditional Indian instruments, including the Mridangam, Tabla, Nashik Dhol, Punjabi Dhol, Chenda, Dholu and Thamate, came together with Africa’s Djembe and Timbales and Australia’s Didgeridoo. Complemented by Liquid Drumming, beatboxing and the flute, the performance brought diverse musical traditions together in a vibrant rhythmic ensemble. Together, the three performances traced an artistic journey from the blossoming of stories and the voice of nature to the shared energy of rhythm. Reflecting the spirit of ‘Stories Without Borders’, the theme of the 57 th edition of the International Film Festival of India, they showcased how dance and music can transcend linguistic and geographical boundaries, bringing diverse cultural expressions together on one stage.
